name: Belmond Savute Elephant Lodge
insider_take: This isn't just a safari lodge—it's front-row seats to one of Africa's greatest wildlife spectacles in the heart of Chobe National Park.
whats_special: Perched along the legendary Savute Channel, this intimate 12-pavilion lodge offers unparalleled access to the famous Savute Marsh, where massive elephant herds gather during seasonal migrations. The channel mysteriously flows and stops for decades at a time—it resumed flowing in 2008 after being dry for 28 years, transforming the landscape and wildlife patterns.
pro_tip: Visit during dry season (May-October) when thousands of elephants converge at the waterhole directly in front of the lodge—you can watch the action unfold from your private deck with morning coffee.
dont_miss: The ancient San rock paintings at Gubatsa Hills, just a short drive away, showcase 4,000-year-old artwork. Also witness the incredible sight of elephants and lions sharing the same watering holes—Savute's lions are uniquely known for hunting young elephants, a rare behavior you won't see elsewhere.
pros: Prime location for elephant viewing in the Savute Channel area
Luxury safari experience with exceptional game drives
Expert guides and naturalists providing wildlife expertise
Exclusive access to Chobe National Park's remote Savute region
cons: Remote wilderness location requires charter flights
Seasonal wildlife activity depends on migration patterns
